providers: Google Search Console page history for sc-domain:routebudget.eu
Italian government transport and fuel sources

method.interpretation: Recovery updates existing Italian intent owners that lost broad page-level visibility after 18 August. It adds operator tools and clearer decision paths without creating new URLs, changing query ownership or claiming search volume.
method.volumePolicy: No volume, ranking, traffic or conversion forecast is inferred. Search Console history proves prior Google exposure for these exact URLs, not total Italian demand.

gscContext.purpose: Improve existing high-loss Italian pages and preserve one URL per intent.

candidates.signalNote: Search Console previously exposed the calculator before the sitewide decline. MASE and European fuel series support a dated sensitivity method rather than a universal fuel price.
candidates.intentBoundary: The calculator owns litres and fuel cost from entered distance, measured consumption and price. The consumption guide owns measurement; the cost-per-km calculator owns the wider mission.
candidates.productFit: RouteBudget can carry the verified fuel input into the released wider route-cost workflow with other supported cost components.
candidates.productBoundary: Neither web calculator nor app supplies a guaranteed live fuel price, future price, route, official tariff or final profitability result.

candidates.signalNote: Search Console previously exposed this exact guide. Current official sources support a measured, segmented input workflow and reject one universal consumption number.
candidates.intentBoundary: The guide owns measurement and interpretation of l/100 km. The fuel calculator owns litres and cost after consumption is known; cost-per-km owns complete mission economics.
candidates.productFit: A measured consumption profile is a relevant input to RouteBudget's released fuel estimate and full route-cost workflow.
candidates.productBoundary: RouteBudget does not read telematics, diagnose a vehicle, provide a universal consumption benchmark or guarantee final fuel use.

candidates.signalNote: Search Console previously exposed this exact calculator. MIT cost families support the completeness check while company inputs remain authoritative for the actual mission.
candidates.intentBoundary: The calculator owns forecast cost per travelled and loaded kilometre for one mission. The historical guide owns period accounting; the margin calculator owns final price scenarios.
candidates.productFit: The result connects directly to RouteBudget's released cost breakdown and scenario workflow without claiming a market tariff.
candidates.productBoundary: RouteBudget does not calculate a live route, official minimum tariff, legal price, tax result or guaranteed margin.

candidates.signalNote: Search Console previously exposed the pillar. The recovery adds an operator go/no-go sequence while retaining the existing complete-trip intent and official cost reference.
candidates.intentBoundary: The pillar owns the complete single-mission cost method. Supporting guides own one component and calculators execute narrower numerical tasks.
candidates.productFit: The method maps to RouteBudget's released complete route calculation, cost breakdown, scenarios and PDF estimate.
candidates.productBoundary: The app does not replace dispatch, routing, live toll lookup, accounting, invoicing, legal review or an official market tariff.

candidates.signalNote: The existing page owns sensitivity analysis. MASE and MIT support dated fuel and cost-family inputs while the update avoids inventing market demand or a universal safety margin.
candidates.intentBoundary: The guide owns residual-margin stress testing after cost and price are known. The price calculator owns coverage threshold, target margin and equivalent markup.
candidates.productFit: RouteBudget's released scenario feature lets an operator compare supported price scenarios after building the mission cost.
candidates.productBoundary: No page or app result guarantees profit, predicts fuel, supplies missing costs or replaces accounting and commercial judgment.
